chunks: From him, from Ayoub, from Safwan, who said: Abu Burdah ibn Rajaa' told me, saying:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a group of people who hand over their land to a man and say to him: 'Consume it and pay its land tax (kharaj).' He said: 'There is no harm with it; if they wish to take it, they may take it.'

key_terms.خَرَاج: Land tax or tribute paid by the tenant
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on leasing land where the tenant pays the fixed tax (kharaj)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the *muzara'ah* contract where the tenant bears the produce and tax burden, emphasizing the owner's retained right of reclamation. This ruling reflects the early Shia juristic consensus on the flexibility of agricultural leases, distinguishing it from stricter views on risk-sharing. The permissibility underscores the principle of contractual freedom (*al-asl fi al-akhdhi*) in civil transactions, provided the terms are mutually agreed upon.
